Increased Body Temperature The hypothalamus is the centre of the thermoregulato- ry system and is responsible for maintaining the body temperature at a set point (known as the set-point temperature) which is normally 37°. Mechanisms that produce or conserve body heat include passive heat absorption from the environment, peripheral vasocon- striction, and thermogenic processes such as metabolic reactions and shivering.
